headline: WaveForge creates beat-synced music videos from your song in about a minute
summary: Independent artists often struggle to create music videos for platforms like TikTok and Reels. WaveForge automates this process, generating beat-synced videos from any song in roughly 60 seconds.
details: Independent artists face a significant challenge in creating music videos for video-first platforms like TikTok and Reels, where visual content is key for discovery. WaveForge addresses this by generating beat-synced music videos from any song in about a minute, eliminating the need for manual editing.

Traditional music video production is often too expensive or time-consuming for most indie artists, requiring professional editors or extensive personal effort to sync cuts to a beat. WaveForge simplifies this by offering a no-timeline, no-keyframes, and no-editing-skills-needed solution.

The developer, Eric Rieds, built WaveForge to empower artists. Users can try their first video for free at waveforge.net, with no credit card required. The creator is actively seeking feedback to refine the platform.

headline: GameBoy runs on E-Paper ESP32 at 30FPS
summary: A custom-built system allows the classic GameBoy to run on an E-Paper display powered by an ESP32 microcontroller, achieving a surprisingly smooth 30 frames per second.
details: A new project demonstrates a classic GameBoy running on an E-Paper display. This setup achieves a surprisingly smooth 30 frames per second, showcasing significant technical ingenuity.
The system utilizes an ESP32 microcontroller to drive the E-Paper screen. This combination allows for a low-power, portable emulation experience.
The video linked in the original source provides a visual demonstration of the GameBoy's performance on this unique display. It highlights the potential for retro gaming on unconventional hardware.
caption:
Imagine playing GameBoy on an E-Paper screen. This project makes it a reality, hitting 30 frames per second!

A new project demonstrates a classic GameBoy running on an E-Paper display. This setup achieves a surprisingly smooth 30 frames per second, showcasing significant technical ingenuity.
